messages.author: eb762f049c898baa
messages.subject: How to create an axis with time units ?
parts:
Dear all,
got a question: I would like to display recordings with "real" time units. Let´s say the recording starts at 19:45:00 and ends at 19:46:30 - this should somehow appear as x labels. Any ideas?
Thanks a lot in advance!
Cheers,
Martin

messages.author: 44c03a0165efd08f
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] How to create an axis with time units ?
parts:
Hi Martin,

I assume you want to plot a spectrogram. One way of doing so is a bit inelegant but works.

If you're using the regular spectro() function, and assuming 'song' is your wave object:

spectro(song, axisX=F)  ##Don't plot the normal x-axis labels
axis(1, labels = format(seq(as.POSIXct("2013-01-01 19:45:00"), as.POSIXct("2013-01-01 19:46:30"), by = "15 s"), "%H:%M:%S"), at = seq(0,90,by = 15)) ## Add in a new axis on the bottom with labels that correspond to the time you want, and at the places you want them to be.

Here, format() is used to display only certain parts of a time/date object. In our case, only the HH:MM:SS, but you can change that.

If you want to be a bit fancier with the labels, you can specify just the start and the breaks:
start <- as.POSIXct("2013-01-01 19:45:00")
axis(1, labels = format(seq(from = start, to = start + length(temp)/te...@samp.rate, by = "15 s"), "%H:%M:%S"), at = seq(0,length(temp)/te...@samp.rate, by = 15))

length(temp) gives you the no. samples
te...@samp.rate gives you the sample rate
Therefore length(temp)/te...@samp.rate gives you the length of the song in seconds.

This would be slightly different using the ggplot2 spectro function, but I haven't had the chance to explore that one yet (but I'm looking forward to it!).

Steffi

messages.author: 44c03a0165efd08f
messages.subject: Re: Aw: Re: [seewave] How to create an axis with time units ?
parts:
I'm glad it worked for you!

Just remember that because you're completely redrawing the axes with out
reference to the actual data, it's really really easy to make things up
by accident. The first time I ran through the script, I accidentally
created labels showing time over 5min when the actual wave file was only
2.5s long!

Steffi
